short: Argentina has no AI law. Several member bills sit in the Chamber of Deputies, and the data protection authority, the AAIP, has issued non-binding AI guidance; Law 25.326 on personal data binds.
title: Argentina AI Laws
subtitle: No AI law: member bills in Congress and non-binding AAIP guidance
body_html:
Status at a glance

No AI act. Argentina has no AI law. Several bills by individual deputies are before the Chamber of Deputies, among them 2130-D-2025, a legal framework for the responsible development and use of AI systems that was on the Science, Technology and Productive Innovation committee's agenda on 16 September 2025, and a 2026 bill by Deputy Juan Fernando Brügge on the legal regime for the responsible use of AI. The Agency for Access to Public Information (AAIP) published a preliminary guide to using AI responsibly on 27 September 2024; it is not binding. Law 25.326 on the protection of personal data binds. Verified on 25 October 2026 against the Chamber of Deputies, InfoLEG and the AAIP.

Key instruments

InstrumentNumberDateStatus
Legal framework for the development, implementation and responsible use of AI systemsBill 2130-D-2025Committee agenda 16 September 2025Member bill
Legal regime for the responsible use of AI in Argentina2026 bill (Dep. Brügge)2026Member bill
Guide to using AI responsibly (preliminary)AAIP27 September 2024Non-binding guidance
Law on the protection of personal dataLey 25.326Sanctioned 4 October 2000In force

Who regulates and enforces

  • Agency for Access to Public Information (AAIP): data protection and AI guidance.
  • The 2026 Brügge bill would make the National Institute of Industrial Technology (INTI) the AI authority (art. 16); it is a proposal.

Scope and reach

No AI statute. The Brügge bill, as proposed, would cover providers, deployers, importers, distributors, manufacturers and users, and exclude research and development before market placement (art. 3).

Core obligations

  • None under an AI law. Law 25.326 governs AI that processes personal data.

Penalties

BreachMaximumProvisionEnforcer
Infringements of Law 25.326A fine of ARS 1,000 to ARS 100,000, with suspension or closure of the database; later regulatory scales were not checkedLey 25.326, art. 31AAIP
Under the 2026 Brügge bill, if enactedFines of 1 to 1,000 "Argentinos Oro" (art. 17)BillINTI, as proposed

What is coming next

Committee work on the AI bills; no date set. The Chamber's bill index is watched weekly.

Related

Sources

Last verified

25 October 2026, against the sources above. Not confirmed on an official source and therefore left out: a November 2025 committee opinion on 2130-D-2025, and an executive bill of May 2026.
